title: C & Low-level Programming
subtitle: Learn what your code actually does to memory — the layer every higher-level language is standing on, and the one attackers work in.
audience: For programmers who can already read simple code in any language and have never had to think about memory, pointers, or what the compiler is doing. No prior C is required — the course teaches the language from the beginning. This course assumes a working Unix-like shell and, from the C course onwards, a C compiler and make. If you do not have those yet — or have never opened a terminal — the Setting Up course installs and verifies all of it first, and nothing here repeats that material.
outcomes: Explain what happens between your source file and a running program
Write C that handles memory deliberately instead of hoping
Read and reason about pointers, including the cases that confuse people
Recognise the memory bugs behind a large share of real vulnerabilities, and find them with tools
Work with bits, integer representation, and floating point without guessing
Build a multi-file project and explain what the linker did
